newsitem.title: CUBA: Date for papal visit to Cuba may be fixed this week.
newsitem.headline: Date for papal visit to Cuba may be fixed this week.

text.p: The date for a planned trip to Cuba by Pope John Paul is likely to be fixed this week during a visit to the island by the chairman of Italy's Roman Catholic Bishops' Conference, Cuban church officials said on Thursday.

Cardinal Camillo Ruini, leading a delegation to visit charitable works supported by the Italian church and meet officials, arrived on Thursday in Havana for a three-day visit. He was met at the airport by Cuba's Cardinal Jaime Ortega and by the papal nuncio (Vatican ambasador) in Cuba, Beniamino Stella.
Ortega told reporters the papal visit -- agreed two months ago but for which a date has not yet been announced -- would be discussed during Ruini's trip.
"We will discuss the visit of the Pope and it is likely that before he leaves, we will have been able to fix a date for the visit, and announce it to you," Ortega said.
Ruini declined comment when asked about a date for the visit.

It was agreed the Pope would travel this year to Cuba, the only Spanish-speaking Latin American country he has not visited, during a historic first meeting last November at the Vatican between the pontiff and President Fidel Castro.

That meeting, which came shortly after a trip to Cuba by Vatican Foreign Minister Jean Louis Tauran, marked a clear improvement in recent months in relations between the island's communist authorities and the Roman Catholic church.

Like Tauran, who visited Cuba last October, Ruini said the Vatican viewed the Cuban Catholic church as being in a phase of renaissance, a process that was helped by a more tolerant attitude on the part of the authorities.

In a statement to reporters at the airport, he said the Catholic Church was enjoying a "clear growth". He added that the meeting between the Pope and Castro, and the announcement the Pope would visit Cuba were "signs of hope".
His own visit, Ruini said, should be another step in what he called "mutual knowledge and normalisation of relations".

Shortly after Castro took control in 1959, Cuba was declared a socialist state. Some 350 Catholic schools were nationalised and more than 100 priests expelled. Freedom of worship and religious instruction are limited to church premises.

Although no date has been announced yet, the pope would be unlikely to come to Cuba in the next few months because of the time required for preparations, and also would not visit during the heat of the Cuban summer. This means a likely time would be during the winter months from October onwards.
Ruini is likely to meet Castro during his visit, but the Cuban leader's engagements are not announced in advance.
He is also due to say mass at Havana cathedral on Friday and to pay brief visits to the eastern cities of Holguin and Santiago de Cuba, before leaving for Haiti on Sunday.
